Definition: to suspend; figuratively (through hesitation) to be uncertain; by implication (of mental dependence) to habituate
BiblicalUsage: Moses warns that in exile a man's life shall hang in doubt before him, and he shall fear day and night, and have no assurance of life. Hosea says the people are bent to backsliding from God, and though they call to the Most High, none at all will exalt Him. The word is to hang suspended, to be uncertain, to lean away: a life hanging in doubt, and a heart bent on leaving.
TheologicalSignificance: Both verses are one warning, I believe: a life that hangs in doubt and a heart bent to backsliding are the same condition, and the cure is the same — to return to the God who knew them in the wilderness.
